titleStmt.title: The Holy Bible, Douay-Rheims Version (original translation): retained structured electronic witness v1.0

publicationStmt.p: Private technical preparation of the complete retained electronic witness, not independent print collation, human acceptance, rights clearance or public publication.

bibl.note: Complete651 extracted textual members of pinnedv1.0; tagged JSON,394annotation sidecars,26reference documents; raw JSON and USFM derivatives retained and accounted separately. ZIP is a package, not textual authority.73canonical+3appendix components; exact duplicate Prayer filename rendered once.

Primary title documents credit the English College of Rheims and the English College of Doway. Gregory Martin and contemporary revisers/annotators are retained configuration attributions, not independently allocated roles.

The release README claims original1582 New Testament and1609-1610 Old Testament. Literal NT title also says fourth Edition1633; OT title also carries1635. No exact historical printed-edition identification or collation is inferred.
The retained README and LICENSE declare CC0 1.0 Universal. This is provider evidence, without independent worldwide clearance or print authenticity proof.

The source release tree does not declare reading order. The established candidate uses an explicitly generated historical Catholic order, then three appendix components. That inherited order is retained, not presented as literal archive order.

Every generated odr-source-field XML ID is SHA256 of its exact original source-json pointer. The manifest-bound complete source field inventory and actual-TEI context companion preserve reversible pointer meaning, original labels and attachment; IDs are not asserted source-supplied identifiers.

Complete pinned v1.0 structured electronic Original Douay-Rheims witness: 651 retained textual members, 77 tagged book files representing 73 canonical books and three appendix components with one exact duplicate Prayer filename accounted once; 394 annotation sidecars, 26 reference documents, and retained raw JSON/USFM derivatives. One existing work and one complete TEI. All 1361 chapters and 37181 source verse occurrences, including both native Tobias 0:0/0:1 carriers, 49 verse-zero labels and one duplicate address, retain literal wording and occurrence identity. Nine omitted chapter articles and 73 misencoded null title fields are repaired from retained source; all other original body bytes invert exactly. Every nonverse node and source-field meaning is delivered in actual-TEI-derived paired context annexes. Generated reading order, provider rights, historical print identity and human/publication decisions remain qualified.
All 73 JSON-null hebrew_title values denote absent fields. Their lexical null accounting is explicitly typed as absence, never an authored language title.

Nine source chapter articles (nine titles, nine texts and 440 subnotes) omitted by the inherited selected-event producer are restored under their own chapter, after the native chapter fields and before separately acquired annotation sidecars. No unrelated historical body text is changed.

The exact source-native zero-chapter policy retains both Tobias 0:0 and 0:1 without renumbering, reference invention or exclusion. Duplicate native verse occurrences retain their original separate IDs.

All actual TEI nonverse nodes, text/tails, inline formatting, source JSON locators and annotation relationships are generated into maintained numbered paired source/data annexes. Generated field IDs are represented by reversible literal source pointers; opaque source-attribute aliases are decoded for human understanding. These context records are not additional Bible verses.
